question: Which biological factor makes women more vulnerable to sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: A higher systemic pH level in the bloodstream
options.B: Reduced microvascular supply to the cervix
options.D: A larger mucosal surface area in the reproductive tract

explanation: The extensive mucosal surface of the female reproductive tract provides a larger area for pathogens to attach and invade during exposure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: An untreated lower genital infection can lead to which major long-term reproductive complication?
explanation: Ascending infections cause scarring and blockage of the fallopian tubes, which is a leading cause of infertility in women. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which STI is caused by a parasite and causes a frothy, yellow-green discharge?
explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan known for causing a characteristic frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge with a foul odor. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which of these pathogens primarily causes genital warts and cervical cancer?
explanation: Human Papillomavirus includes specific genotypes that cause benign warts as well as oncogenic strains linked to cervical malignancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why do many women with chlamydia infections fail to seek early medical treatment?

options.A: Symptoms only appear during post-menopausal years
options.B: The infection often causes no noticeable symptoms in the early stages
options.C: The pathogen immediately destroys all nerve endings in the cervix
options.D: Immune cells quickly clear the bacteria without intervention

explanation: Asymptomatic infections provide no physical warning signs, meaning individuals feel healthy and have no reason to seek clinical care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is a major consequence of leaving asymptomatic infections untreated over a long period?

options.A: Silent damage to the upper reproductive organs
options.C: Immediate regeneration of damaged fallopian tissues
options.D: Complete elimination of normal vaginal flora

explanation: Pathogens can ascend and cause chronic inflammation and scarring in the fallopian tubes and uterus without causing acute pain. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h3)

question: What bedside test involves mixing vaginal secretions with saline to check for moving parasites?
explanation: Wet mount preparation allows direct microscopic visualization of live trichomonads and cellular changes right at the point of care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which diagnostic method is standard for screening systemic infections like syphilis during routine antenatal care?
explanation: Blood-based serological tests detect antibodies or antigens circulating systemically, making them ideal for diagnosing blood-borne and systemic pathogens. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h4)

question: How should a nurse approach giving a positive infection diagnosis during counselling?

options.A: By focusing solely on the financial cost of the medications
options.B: With strict clinical detachment to maintain professional boundaries
options.C: With empathy, confidentiality, and a non-judgmental attitude
options.D: By immediately notifying family members to ensure compliance

explanation: Creating a safe, supportive space reduces the fear of stigma and encourages the patient to engage openly with the treatment plan. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: What key instruction regarding sexual activity must be included in infection counseling?

options.A: Use oil-based lubricants to reduce mucosal friction during therapy
options.B: Switch to barrier methods only after the third dose of medication
options.C: Continue regular intercourse while taking oral antibiotics
options.D: Abstain from sexual intercourse until treatment is finished and symptoms clear

explanation: Temporary abstinence prevents reinfection and allows irritated mucosal tissues time to heal properly. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is treating only the female patient without addressing her sexual partner discouraged?

options.A: It frequently results in a rapid reinfection cycle
options.B: It causes immediate resistance to oral antibiotic therapies
options.C: It accelerates the breakdown of normal vaginal microbiota
options.D: It violates international medical documentation standards

explanation: If the partner remains untreated, unprotected sexual contact will quickly reintroduce the pathogen to the index patient. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of expedited partner therapy in resource-limited settings?

options.A: To eliminate the requirement for patient confidentiality
options.B: To bypass the need for any clinical history taking
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory investigations
options.D: To provide medication to partners who cannot easily visit the clinic

explanation: Expedited therapy allows treatment to reach partners who face logistical barriers, breaking the chain of transmission effectively. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is a major clinical risk when a patient stops taking her antibiotics early because symptoms disappeared?

options.A: Development of antimicrobial resistance and persistent infection
options.B: Permanent suppression of the bone marrow

explanation: Stopping medication prematurely leaves the hardiest pathogens alive, allowing them to mutate, survive, and develop drug resistance. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why are follow-up visits scheduled after completing an antimicrobial treatment course?

options.A: To switch the patient to a different drug class
options.B: To perform a routine surgical biopsy of the cervix
options.C: To renew the prescription for prophylactic use
options.D: To confirm that the infection has been completely cured

explanation: Follow-up testing verifies eradication of the pathogen and ensures treatment success, especially in high-risk groups. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h7)

question: What primary prevention tool provides dual protection against both pregnancy and infections?
explanation: Condoms physically block pathogen transmission while simultaneously preventing sperm from reaching the ovum. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of community-wide health education regarding reproductive infections?

options.A: To empower individuals with knowledge to reduce risky behaviors
options.B: To mandate universal screening for all citizens annually
options.C: To eliminate the prescription of antimicrobial medications
options.D: To replace the need for clinical laboratory diagnostics

explanation: Education equips people to make informed choices, recognize early warning signs, and adopt protective practices. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h8)
